new_steps.cat: Step 4 · Verbs: from dictionary form up

drill.note: The only two irregulars in the language — and する is not just an exception, it is the machine that turns nouns into verbs. 来る moves its reading (きます・こない) while the kanji stands still. The drill is the two machines.

items.q: 毎晩、日本語を勉強___。
items.en: I study Japanese every night.
items.why: 勉強 + する — the noun-to-verb machine.

items.q: 友達に電話___した。
items.en: I phoned a friend.
items.why: 電話する — a call, verbed.

items.q: 明日、友達が___ます。
items.en: A friend is coming tomorrow.
items.why: 来る → きます: the reading moves, the kanji doesn't.

items.q: 昨日は___ませんでした。
items.en: He didn't come yesterday.
items.why: きません — the ます-stem stays き; こ belongs to ない.

items.q: 彼は___ないと思います。
items.en: I don't think he'll come.
items.why: 来ない reads こない — the negative stem is こ.

drill.note: が turns up exactly where English swears there should be an object: understanding, wanting, ability, likes. The reflex to drill: わかる・ほしい・できる・好き all take が, not を.

items.q: 日本語___わかります。
items.en: I understand Japanese.
items.why: わかる takes が — the English object instinct is the trap.

items.q: 新しいくつ___ほしいです。
items.en: I want new shoes.
items.why: ほしい is an adjective; its target takes が.

items.q: 妹はピアノ___できます。
items.en: My sister can play the piano.
items.why: できる takes が.

items.q: 私は犬___好きです。
items.en: I like dogs.
items.why: 好き is a な-adjective — が, never を.

items.q: パン___食べます。
items.en: I eat bread — a real object, for contrast.
items.why: 食べる is a plain action verb — を keeps its job.

seg: THE POINT — went all the way: irreversible, and the verb carries how you feel about it
teshimau.note: One ending, two flavours sharing a root — the action went ALL THE WAY. Neutrally: completion. Emotionally: a result you can't take back, regret included.

wr.t: Casual speech contracts it: 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう, 〜でしまう → 〜じゃう. 忘れちゃった is the same regret at kitchen-table register.
wr.jp: かさを忘れちゃった。
wr.en: I went and forgot my umbrella.

items.q: 宿題を全部やって___ました。
items.en: I got the homework completely done.
items.why: Completion — every bit, through to the end.

items.q: 電車の中でかさを忘れて___ました。
items.en: I went and forgot my umbrella on the train.
items.why: Regret — gone, and the verb says how that feels.

items.q: ケーキを全部食べ___った。
items.en: I ate the whole cake (oops).
items.why: 食べちゃった — the casual contraction of てしまった.

items.q: ホテルを予約して___ました。
items.en: I booked the hotel ahead of time.
items.why: Preparation for later → ておく, not てしまう.

items.q: 大事な書類をなくして___ました。
items.en: I lost the important documents — and can't undo it.
items.why: The irreversible loss — てしまう's emotional home.

seg: THE POINT — done now, for later: the preparation lives inside the verb
teoku.note: An action done in advance so later goes smoothly. 置く, to place — the act set down now, waiting where the future will need it.

wr.t: Casual speech contracts ておく to とく: 買っとく, やっとく — the same forethought, quicker on the tongue.
wr.jp: 飲み物、買っとくね。
wr.en: I'll get the drinks in (for later).

items.q: ホテルを予約して___ました。
items.en: I booked the hotel ahead.
items.why: Now, for later — the later is in the verb's mind.

items.q: 飲み物を冷やして___いてください。
items.en: Please chill the drinks for when they're needed.
items.why: 冷やしておいて — arrangement in advance.

items.q: 会議の前に、資料を読んで___きます。
items.en: I'll read the materials before the meeting.
items.why: Preparation aimed at a known later.

items.q: 窓が開けて___ります。
items.en: The window stands open — someone arranged it.
items.why: The arranged STATE is てある; ておく is the arranging.

items.q: 電気をつけて___きましょう。
items.en: Let's leave the light on (for when we're back).
items.why: つけておく — the future thanked us in advance.

seg: the window — が, because the state is the news
open — transitive 開ける in て form
THE POINT — the state stands, and somebody made it on purpose
tearu.note: A state that exists because somebody deliberately arranged it. The transitive verb betrays the hidden arranger; the が puts the state on stage.

wr.t: The minimal pair with ている: 電気がついています (state, no story — intransitive) vs 電気がつけてあります (state with intent — transitive). The verb's transitivity is the whole tell.
wr.jp: 電気がつけてあります。
wr.en: The light has been left on — on purpose.

items.q: 窓が開けて___ます。
items.en: The window stands open — someone opened it on purpose.
items.why: The arranged state → てある.

items.q: 晩ご飯はもう作って___ます。
items.en: Dinner's already made — someone saw to it.
items.why: The state waits, intent visible in it.

items.q: 電気がついて___ます。
items.en: The light is on — just a state, no story.
items.why: Intransitive つく + ている — nobody claimed.

items.q: ドアにメモがはって___ます。
items.en: A note has been posted on the door.
items.why: はる is transitive; the posting was deliberate.

items.q: パーティーの飲み物は冷やして___ます。
items.en: The party drinks are chilled and waiting.
items.why: Someone chilled them for this — てある reports the readiness.

drill.note: Four continuations of て, one clean division: ている (ongoing or state), てある (a state someone arranged), ておく (arranging now for later), てしまう (went all the way, sometimes regrettably). The light switch demonstrates all four.

items.q: 電気がついて___ます。
items.en: The light is on — state, no story.
items.why: Intransitive + ている.

items.q: 電気がつけて___ます。
items.en: The light is on — someone left it on deliberately.
items.why: Transitive + てある — intent in the state.

items.q: 電気をつけて___きます。
items.en: I'll put the light on for later.
items.why: ておく — the arranging itself.

items.q: 電気を消し忘れて___ました。
items.en: I went and forgot to switch the light off.
items.why: てしまう — done, regrettably.

items.q: 宿題はもうやって___ますから、遊べます。
items.en: The homework's already done (taken care of), so I can play.
items.why: The arranged state, standing ready.

new_steps.cat: Step 40 · Regret, hope, and the unreal

seg: if I had left — the ば of Step 38's ばいい
THE POINT — it would have been good: the road not taken, regretted in grammar
bayokatta.note: ばいい in the past becomes the thing you did not do. The regret is in the grammar, so your voice doesn't have to carry it.

wr.t: English flips the auxiliary; Japanese flips the VERB: I shouldn't have said it is 言わなければよかった — it would have been good had I not said it.
wr.jp: あんなこと、言わなければよかった。
wr.en: I shouldn't have said that.

items.q: もっと早く出れ___よかった。
items.en: I should have left earlier.
items.why: The ばよかった frame — ば, always.

items.q: あんなこと、言わなけれ___よかった。
items.en: I shouldn't have said that.
items.why: The negative regret — the verb flips, not the auxiliary.

items.q: 傘を持ってくれ___よかったですね。
items.en: We should have brought an umbrella.
items.why: 持ってくればよかった — shared regret, same frame.

items.q: 明日、晴れる___いいですね。
items.en: I hope it's fine tomorrow — a wish, not a regret.
items.why: 晴れるといい — hope for the future; ばよかった only looks back.

items.q: 聞け___よかった。
items.en: I should have asked.
items.why: The learner's most-used regret.

seg: THE POINT — 'I hope': the wish, out of your hands
ね — inviting them to hope along
taraii.note: One shape, two readings, split by what follows: with ね/な it is a WISH about what you can't control; as a question (どうしたらいい？) it asks for the easy answer.

wr.t: どうしたらいいですか is the question form — Step 38's ばいい wearing たら. The wish and the request for advice share one machine.
wr.jp: どうしたらいいですか。
wr.en: What should I do?

items.q: 明日、晴れる___いいですね。
items.en: I hope it's fine tomorrow.
items.why: The wish about the uncontrollable → といい.

items.q: どうし___いいですか。
items.en: What should I do?
items.why: The advice question — したらいい.

items.q: 早く良くなる___いいね。
items.en: Hope you get better soon.
items.why: Health is not yours to control — the wish form.

items.q: もっと早く出れば___。
items.en: I should have left earlier — regret, for contrast.
items.why: Past + ば → regret; present + と → wish.

items.q: 試験に受かる___いいなあ。
items.en: I so hope I pass the exam.
items.why: な after いい — the wish said half to yourself.

seg: THE POINT — 'supposing': an if about the ARGUMENT, not the world
we've got a problem — what follows from the granted premise
toshitara.note: Grants a premise for the sake of what follows. Not predicting it's true — arguing from it. とすれば is the same hinge, one shade more written.

wr.t: The interview classic runs on it: 一億円もらうとしたら、何をしますか — nobody thinks you'll get the money; the premise is granted purely to see what you'd do inside it.
wr.jp: 一億円もらうとしたら、何をしますか。
wr.en: Supposing you got a hundred million yen, what would you do?

items.q: 本当だ___、大変です。
items.en: If that's true, we've got a problem.
items.why: The premise granted for argument's sake.

items.q: 行く___、来週でしょう。
items.en: If we're going at all, it'd be next week.
items.why: The written shade of the same supposing.

items.q: 一億円もらう___、何をしますか。
items.en: Supposing you got 100 million yen — what would you do?
items.why: Pure hypothesis, granted to explore.

items.q: 雨が降っ___、中止です。
items.en: If it rains, it's cancelled — a real-world if.
items.why: An ordinary condition about the world → たら; としたら argues.

items.q: 引っ越す___、どこがいいですか。
items.en: Supposing you moved — where would be good?
items.why: The move isn't planned; the premise is borrowed.

seg: worry — the classical せ stem of する
THE POINT — cannot BE without doing it: the feeling overrides you
zuniwairarenai.note: Not 'couldn't stop' — could not exist without doing it. The ず is the old negative, surviving exactly here; する takes its classical stem: 心配せず.

wr.t: する reaches back for せ: 心配せずには, 参加せずには — the same classical stem rule that ざるを得ない will confirm in Stage 12. Learn it once here.
wr.jp: この話を聞くと、笑わずにはいられない。
wr.en: Hearing this, you can't help laughing.

items.q: 彼女のことを心配___にはいられません。
items.en: I can't help worrying about her.
items.why: する → せず — the classical stem.

items.q: この話を聞くと、笑わ___にはいられない。
items.en: Hearing this, you can't help laughing.
items.why: 笑わず + にはいられない — the frame's negative.

items.q: 言わ___にはいられなかった。
items.en: I couldn't keep it in.
items.why: The urge won; the old negative records it.

items.q: 泣か___にはいられなかった。
items.en: I couldn't not cry.
items.why: The overriding feeling, in the ず frame.

items.q: セールと聞いて、見___にはいられなかった。
items.en: Hearing 'sale', I couldn't not look.
items.why: 見ずにはいられない — compulsion, confessed.

seg: THE POINT — the weakest claim the language makes: intuition, marked as intuition
younakigasuru.note: Below かもしれない, below はず, below と思う — a sense you cannot back up and are DECLARING you cannot back up. Honesty about the evidence, built into the ending.

wr.t: 気がする alone (without ような) claims a shade more: 忘れている気がする leans toward believing it. The ような is the extra step back.
wr.jp: 何か忘れているような気がします。
wr.en: I feel like I'm forgetting something.

items.q: どこかで会った___気がします。
items.en: I feel like we've met somewhere.
items.why: The declared intuition → ような気がする.

items.q: 少し寒くなった___気がする。
items.en: I have a feeling it's got a bit colder.
items.why: A sense, unbackable, and marked so.

items.q: 何か忘れている___気がします。
items.en: I feel like I'm forgetting something.
items.why: The pre-departure classic.

items.q: 電気が消えている。もう帰った___。
items.en: Lights off — he MUST have gone home: evidence, not intuition.
items.why: Evidence closes upward → に違いない; 気がする has nothing to stand on.

items.q: この道、前に来た___気がする。
items.en: I feel like I've been down this road before.
items.why: Déjà vu — intuition's home ground.

seg: THE POINT — the flag: what follows is frankly not the case
like — the comparison まるで just made honest
marude.note: ようだ alone can mean 'it seems'; まるで in front removes that reading — the comparison is frank, and both parties know it isn't so.

wr.t: みたい carries the casual register of the same frame: まるで冬みたいに寒い — winter-like cold, said over coffee rather than on paper.
wr.jp: まるで冬みたいに寒いですね。
wr.en: It's cold, like winter.

items.q: ___夢のようです。
items.en: It's like a dream.
items.why: The frank-comparison flag.

items.q: まるで子供の___喜んでいます。
items.en: He's delighted, like a child.
items.why: まるで〜ように — the pair, adverbial.

items.q: まるで冬___に寒いですね。
items.en: Cold like winter.
items.why: The casual cut of the frame.

items.q: 彼は何も聞いていない___に、仕事を続けた。
items.en: He kept working as if he'd heard nothing — Stage 12's contrary-to-fact, for contrast.
items.why: かのようだ seals contrary-to-fact; まるで merely flags the frank simile.

items.q: ___先生のように話しますね。
items.en: You talk just like a teacher.
items.why: The flag again — plainly not a teacher, delightedly compared.

drill.note: Four unrealities, not interchangeable: ばよかった (regret — didn't do it), といい (wish — out of your hands), としたら (premise — granted to argue), まるで〜ようだ (comparison — frankly not so). Read which unreality you're holding.

items.q: 聞け___よかった。
items.en: Regret — I should have asked.
items.why: The road not taken → ばよかった.

items.q: 晴れる___いいですね。
items.en: Wish — out of our hands.
items.why: Hope for the uncontrollable → といい.

items.q: 本当だ___、困ります。
items.en: Premise — granted for the argument.
items.why: Arguing from a supposition.

items.q: ___夢のようだ。
items.en: Comparison — frankly not so.
items.why: The frank simile flag.

items.q: 会った___気がする。
items.en: And the weakest claim of all — intuition, marked.
items.why: ような気がする — unbackable, and honest about it.

seg: THE POINT — covered in it, and it's a mess: the judgement is baked in
darake.note: Full of something, and the something is always unwelcome — mud, mistakes, scratches. No adjective needed; the disapproval is in the suffix.

wr.t: Abstract messes qualify too: 間違いだらけの作文, 借金だらけの生活 — the suffix doesn't care whether the mud is literal.
wr.jp: この作文は間違いだらけです。
wr.en: This composition is riddled with mistakes.

items.q: 靴が泥___になりました。
items.en: My shoes got covered in mud.
items.why: Unwelcome coverage → だらけ.

items.q: この作文は間違い___です。
items.en: Riddled with mistakes.
items.why: The abstract mud.

items.q: 傷___の手をしていた。
items.en: His hands were covered in scratches.
items.why: Coverage, unwelcome, visible.

items.q: そのシャツ、安___ね。
items.en: That shirt looks cheap — approximation, not coverage.
items.why: -ish → っぽい; だらけ needs a substance or a swarm.

items.q: 部屋がほこり___だ。
items.en: The room is thick with dust.
items.why: Dust everywhere — the suffix tuts as it describes.

seg: THE POINT — '-ish': somewhat like, casually, and usually unflatteringly
ppoi.note: The most productive suffix in casual Japanese: 子供っぽい, 忘れっぽい, 白っぽい. Somewhat-like, attached to almost anything, rarely as a compliment.

wr.t: On verb stems it means prone-to: 忘れっぽい, 飽きっぽい — がち's casual cousin, worn as a personal trait rather than a pattern.
wr.jp: 最近、忘れっぽくなりました。
wr.en: I've got forgetful lately.

items.q: そのシャツ、安___ね。
items.en: That shirt looks cheap.
items.why: Cheap-ish — the casual approximation.

items.q: 最近、忘れ___くなりました。
items.en: I've got forgetful lately.
items.why: The prone-to reading on a stem.

items.q: ちょっと子供___ですね。
items.en: That's a bit childish.
items.why: Child-like, and not admiringly.

items.q: 靴が泥___になった。
items.en: Shoes covered in mud — coverage, not resemblance.
items.why: A substance everywhere → だらけ.

items.q: この水、少し茶色___ですね。
items.en: This water looks a bit brownish.
items.why: Color-ish — っぽい's gentlest job.

seg: THE POINT — hard to bring yourself to: the resistance is inside you
gatai.note: にくい is physically awkward; がたい is resistance of the heart — 信じがたい, 捨てがたい, 忘れがたい. A small, mostly fixed set, all interior.

wr.t: The living members are few: 信じがたい, 捨てがたい, 忘れがたい, 理解しがたい, 許しがたい. Treat it as a closed shelf, not a productive machine.
wr.jp: この本は捨てがたいです。
wr.en: I can't quite bring myself to throw this book out.

items.q: 信じ___話ですね。
items.en: That's a hard story to believe.
items.why: The believing resists from inside → がたい.

items.q: この本は捨て___です。
items.en: I can't bring myself to toss this book.
items.why: Attachment, not awkwardness.

items.q: 忘れ___一日でした。
items.en: An unforgettable day.
items.why: The heart refuses the forgetting.

items.q: このふたは固くて、開け___です。
items.en: This lid is stiff and hard to open — physical.
items.why: Mechanical difficulty → にくい; がたい would claim feelings about the jar.

items.q: 彼の行動は理解し___。
items.en: His behavior is hard to comprehend.
items.why: 理解しがたい — the fixed-shelf member.

seg: THE POINT — more than can be got through: きる negated into overflow
kirenai.note: きる meant all-the-way-through; きれない is the useful half — the quantity defeats the finishing. 数えきれない stars, 読みきれない books.

wr.t: ほど loves the frame: 数えきれないほど星がある — stars past counting, the overflow measured by its own uncountability.
wr.jp: 数えきれないほど星があります。
wr.en: There are more stars than you could count.

items.q: 多すぎて、食べ___ません。
items.en: It's too much — I can't finish it.
items.why: Quantity defeats completion → きれない.

items.q: 数え___ないほど星があります。
items.en: More stars than you could count.
items.why: The uncountable, counted honestly.

items.q: 読み___ないほど本があります。
items.en: More books than I could get through.
items.why: The pile wins.

items.q: 最後まで走り___ました。
items.en: Ran it all the way — the positive きる, for contrast.
items.why: Completion against difficulty → ぬく; きれない is the defeat.

items.q: 感謝の気持ちは言葉では言い___ません。
items.en: My gratitude is more than words can carry.
items.why: 言いきれない — the feeling overflows the sentence.

seg: THE POINT — and nothing since: the hard edge after the last event
kiri.note: Two senses, one hard edge: ONLY of a small number (二人きり), and SINCE with nothing after (出て行ったきり). 寝たきり — bedridden — is the second sense fossilized.

wr.t: The only-sense makes intimacy: 二人きりで話したい — just the two of us, the edge drawn around the pair on purpose.
wr.jp: 二人きりで話したいです。
wr.en: I'd like to talk with just the two of us.

items.q: 彼は出て行った___、帰ってきません。
items.en: He went out and hasn't come back since.
items.why: The last event, edge hard, nothing after.

items.q: 二人___で話したいです。
items.en: Just the two of us.
items.why: The only-sense, drawn close.

items.q: 祖母は寝た___です。
items.en: My grandmother is bedridden.
items.why: 寝たきり — the since-sense fossilized into a word.

items.q: 朝コーヒーを飲んだ___、何も食べていません。
items.en: Coffee this morning — nothing since.
items.why: The hard edge after the last intake.

items.q: 窓を開けた___にして寝てしまった。
items.en: Left the window open and fell asleep — the left-that-way is っぱなし territory.
items.why: Unattended state → っぱなし; きり marks the edge after a last event.

seg: THE POINT — one direction only, and not stopping: the slide with no second gear
ippouda.note: A change running one way with no sign of turning. ようになる noted a change happened; 一方だ says it is STILL happening and only ever that way.

wr.t: Stage 14's ばかりだ will do the same one-way slide with a darker face; 一方だ is the neutral instrument — the graph line, not the groan.
wr.jp: 人口は減る一方だ。
wr.en: The population only ever falls.

items.q: 物価は上がる___です。
items.en: Prices just keep going up.
items.why: One direction, no turning → 一方だ.

items.q: 人口は減る___だ。
items.en: The population only ever falls.
items.why: The graph line, still sliding.

items.q: 仕事が増える___で、休めません。
items.en: The work only piles up, and I can't rest.
items.why: The slide, lived inside.

items.q: 最近、忘れ___です。
items.en: I've been forgetful lately — a tendency, not a slide.
items.why: Recurring episodes → がち; 一方 needs a continuous direction.

items.q: 円は安くなる___です。
items.en: The yen only keeps weakening.
items.why: One-way currency, one-way grammar.

drill.note: The suffixes, sorted: だらけ (unwelcome abundance), っぽい (approximate, unflattering), がたい (inner resistance), きれない (quantity defeats finishing), きり (hard edge — only / nothing-since), 一方だ (one direction, not stopping). English needs whole phrases; these clip on.

items.q: 泥___です。
items.en: Unwelcome abundance.
items.why: Coverage in the unwelcome.

items.q: 安___です。
items.en: Approximate, and unflattering.
items.why: -ish.

items.q: 上がる___です。
items.en: One direction, and not a good one.
items.why: The unbroken slide.

items.q: 信じ___です。
items.en: The heart resists it.
items.why: Interior difficulty.

items.q: 食べ___ません。
items.en: More than can be finished.
items.why: Quantity wins.

seg: hot — the state that will not last
THE POINT — while it lasts: a window that is going to close
召し上がってください。
please eat — keigo, as the table demands
uchini.note: The expiry is the whole difference from 間に: 間 is just a span; うちに is a closing window, and the unspoken half is hurry.

wr.t: ないうちに flips the window: 忘れないうちに — before the forgetting arrives; 暗くならないうちに — before the light goes. The closing thing can be an absence.
wr.jp: 忘れないうちにメモします。
wr.en: I'll note it down before I forget.

items.q: 熱い___に召し上がってください。
items.en: Please eat it while it's hot.
items.why: The heat is a closing window → うちに.

items.q: 忘れない___にメモします。
items.en: I'll note it down before I forget.
items.why: Before the window shuts on memory.

items.q: 明るい___に帰りましょう。
items.en: Let's head back while it's light.
items.why: Daylight expires; うちに says so.

items.q: 夏休みの___、毎日プールに行きました。
items.en: During summer break I swam daily — a neutral span.
items.why: No expiry pressure → 間; うちに would add a race.

items.q: 若い___に、いろいろな国を見たいです。
items.en: While I'm young, I want to see many countries.
items.why: Youth is the classic closing window.

seg: THE POINT — every single time, without exception
tabini.note: Not whenever-it-happens — EVERY time, reliably, no exceptions on record. The recurrence itself is the claim.

wr.t: Nouns join with の: 試験のたびに緊張する — each exam, the same nerves, the record unbroken.
wr.jp: 試験のたびに緊張します。
wr.en: I get nervous every single exam.

items.q: この歌を聞く___に、国を思い出します。
items.en: Every time I hear this song, I think of home.
items.why: Unbroken recurrence → たびに.

items.q: 会う___に、背が伸びていますね。
items.en: You've grown every time I see you.
items.why: Each meeting, the same discovery.

items.q: 試験___たびに緊張します。
items.en: Every exam, the nerves.
items.why: Noun + のたびに.

items.q: 買い物の___に、郵便局に寄りました。
items.en: I dropped by the post office while out shopping — a carried errand, not a recurrence.
items.why: One trip, second errand → ついでに.

items.q: 引っ越しの___に、物を捨てます。
items.en: Every time I move, I throw things out.
items.why: The reliable ritual of every move.

seg: the shopping — the real reason for the trip
THE POINT — while at it: the second errand rides the first
dropped by the post office — the passenger
tsuideni.note: The first action is the trip's real reason; the second is a passenger — and the pattern says so, which keeps the favor small.

wr.t: Sentence-initial it softens requests: ついでにこれもお願い — since you're going anyway. The favor borrows the trip's momentum and stays polite by staying small.
wr.jp: ついでにこれもお願いできますか。
wr.en: Could you do this too while you're at it?

items.q: 買い物の___に、郵便局に寄りました。
items.en: Dropped by the post office while out shopping.
items.why: The second errand rides the first.

items.q: ___にこれもお願いできますか。
items.en: Could you do this too while you're at it?
items.why: The small favor on borrowed momentum.

items.q: 散歩の___にパンを買ってきます。
items.en: I'll pick up bread on my walk.
items.why: The walk is the trip; the bread is the passenger.

items.q: この歌を聞く___に、国を思い出します。
items.en: Every time I hear this song — recurrence, not errand.
items.why: Every-time → たびに.

items.q: 駅へ行く___に、この手紙を出してくれますか。
items.en: On your way to the station, could you post this?
items.why: The errand hitches onto a trip already happening.

seg: having actually lived — て form, tried
THE POINT — only then, and not before: the knowledge needed the experience
tehajimete.note: The realisation that requires the doing: the knowledge was unavailable in advance, which is a stronger claim than 'I learned it late'.

wr.t: The proverb-shaped uses carry the pattern's heart: 失って初めて、大切さに気づく — only in losing it do you see what it was worth.
wr.jp: 失って初めて、大切さに気づきます。
wr.en: You only realise the value once it's gone.

items.q: 日本に住んでみて___、分かりました。
items.en: I didn't really understand until I lived in Japan.
items.why: The knowledge needed the living.

items.q: 失って___、大切さに気づきます。
items.en: Only once it's gone do you see its worth.
items.why: The realisation that requires the loss.

items.q: 自分でやって___、難しさが分かった。
items.en: Only doing it myself showed me how hard it was.
items.why: Experience as the only teacher.

items.q: 親になって___、親の気持ちが分かりました。
items.en: Only on becoming a parent did I understand my parents.
items.why: The unavailable-in-advance knowledge.

items.q: 話し合った___、こうなりました。
items.en: After discussion, this is where we landed — an outcome, not a realisation.
items.why: Deliberate process → 結果; て初めて needs a dawning.

seg: THE POINT — as a result of it: the outcome, reported
kekka.note: The written register's because-therefore: the outcome of a DELIBERATE process. Reports, minutes, announcements — where outcomes need their process shown.

wr.t: その結果 stands sentence-initial and carries a whole paragraph's causality: the process described, then その結果, then what came of it.
wr.jp: その結果、参加者が増えました。
wr.en: As a result, attendance rose.

items.q: よく話し合った___、こうなりました。
items.en: After a good discussion, this is where we landed.
items.why: Deliberate process, reported outcome.

items.q: 調査の___、原因が分かりました。
items.en: The investigation identified the cause.
items.why: 調査の結果 — the report's own hinge.

items.q: その___、参加者が増えました。
items.en: As a result, attendance rose.
items.why: The sentence-initial carrier.

items.q: 雪の___、電車が遅れています。
items.en: Trains delayed because of snow — a cause, not a process.
items.why: ために takes causes; 結果 wants deliberation behind it.

items.q: 練習を続けた___、大会で優勝できました。
items.en: The continued practice ended in a tournament win.
items.why: The earned outcome, with its process named.

seg: THE POINT — in order to: purpose, because the verb is volitional
tameni.note: One shape, two jobs, split by control: a volitional verb in front makes PURPOSE (勉強するために); a noun or uncontrolled event makes CAUSE (雪のために).

wr.t: The cause reading is the announcement register: 事故のため、電車が遅れています — because of, with no one's intention anywhere in it.
wr.jp: 事故のため、電車が遅れています。
wr.en: Trains are delayed because of an accident.

items.q: 日本語を勉強する___に来ました。
items.en: I came in order to study Japanese.
items.why: Volitional verb → purpose.

items.q: 事故の___、電車が遅れています。
items.en: Delayed because of an accident.
items.why: Uncontrolled cause — the announcement's voice.

items.q: 家族の___に働いています。
items.en: I work for my family's sake.
items.why: For-the-sake-of — purpose with a beneficiary.

items.q: 健康の___に、毎朝走っています。
items.en: I run every morning for my health.
items.why: The purpose reading on a noun of aim.

items.q: 台風の___、学校が休みになりました。
items.en: School was closed because of the typhoon.
items.why: Cause — nobody intended the typhoon.

drill.note: The rest of when, fine-grained: 間に (neutral span), うちに (closing window), たびに (reliable recurrence), ついでに (carried errand), て初めて (knowledge that needed the experience). The drill reads which when the sentence holds.

items.q: 熱い___にどうぞ。
items.en: The window is closing.
items.why: Expiry pressure → うちに.

items.q: 会う___に大きくなるね。
items.en: Every occurrence, without exception.
items.why: The unbroken record.

items.q: 住んで___分かりました。
items.en: The knowledge needed the experience.
items.why: Only-then.

items.q: 散歩の___にパンを買った。
items.en: The errand rode the walk.
items.why: The passenger errand.

items.q: 留守の___に、荷物が届きました。
items.en: The parcel came while I was out — a neutral span.
items.why: No window, no recurrence — just the span.

seg: THE POINT — 'in other words': the restatement, opening the sentence
is what you mean? — the package, checked back
tsumari.note: Says the same thing again, shorter and clearer — and lets a learner CHECK understanding by restating. The single most useful connector in the room.

wr.t: It pairs with ということ constantly: つまり〜ということですか — the restatement offered as a question, which is how you verify without accusing anyone of being unclear.
wr.jp: つまり、行けないんですね。
wr.en: In other words, you can't come.

items.q: ___、明日は休みということですか。
items.en: So what you mean is tomorrow's off?
items.why: The restatement check.

items.q: ___、行けないんですね。
items.en: In other words, you can't come.
items.why: The shorter, clearer again.

items.q: ___、そういうことです。
items.en: That, in short, is the situation.
items.why: The summary stamp.

items.q: 早く出ました。___、間に合いませんでした。
items.en: I left early. And yet I didn't make it — the overturn, not the restatement.
items.why: Broken expectation → ところが.

items.q: 毎日五時に起きます。___、朝型なんです。
items.en: I get up at five daily — in other words, a morning person.
items.why: The facts, restated as their meaning.

seg: I left early — the expectation, set
THE POINT — 'and yet': the turn the speaker did not see coming
間に合いませんでした。
tokoroga.note: Sentence-initial but, specifically the SURPRISING one: what follows overturned an expectation the speaker actually held. でも is neutral; ところが gasps.

wr.t: The overturn must be real: if you expected the failure, ところが rings false and でも or しかし is honest. The pattern spends your surprise — have some.
wr.jp: 安いと思いました。ところが、高かった。
wr.en: I thought it'd be cheap. It wasn't.

items.q: 早く出ました。___、間に合いませんでした。
items.en: I left early. And yet I didn't make it.
items.why: The held expectation, overturned.

items.q: ___、誰も来なかったんです。
items.en: But then — nobody came.
items.why: The story's gasp.

items.q: 安いと思いました。___、高かった。
items.en: I thought it'd be cheap. It wasn't.
items.why: Expectation named, then broken.

items.q: 私は反対です。___、時間がないからです。
items.en: I'm against it — the reason being there's no time.
items.why: Claim-then-reason → なぜなら.

items.q: 雨の予報でした。___、快晴でした。
items.en: Rain was forecast. And yet — clear skies.
items.why: The forecast believed, the sky disagreeing.

seg: it's gotten convenient — one true thing
THE POINT — on the other hand: both held, deliberately
人と話さなくなりました。
we talk less — the other true thing
ippoude.note: Two true things about one subject, pulling different ways — a balance stated deliberately, which is what fair writing is made of. Not 反面's single-coin split (that's Stage 14); 一方で can hold separate arenas.

wr.t: Sentence-initial 一方、 pivots a whole paragraph to the other side of the ledger: 給料はいい。一方、休みが少ない。
wr.jp: 給料はいい。一方、休みが少ない。
wr.en: The pay is good. On the other hand, little time off.

items.q: 便利になった___で、人と話さなくなりました。
items.en: Convenient — and on the other hand, we talk less.
items.why: Both true, held in balance.

items.q: 父は厳しい___で、優しいところもあります。
items.en: Strict, but with a kind side too.
items.why: The two-sided portrait.

items.q: 給料はいい。___、休みが少ない。
items.en: Good pay. On the other hand, little rest.
items.why: The ledger's pivot, sentence-initial.

items.q: 物価は上がる___です。
items.en: Prices only ever rise — the one-way slide, for contrast.
items.why: Same word, different machine: 上がる一方だ is the slide; 一方で balances.

items.q: この町は静かな___で、少し不便です。
items.en: Quiet — and on the other hand, a bit inconvenient.
items.why: The honest review's grammar.

seg: I'm against it — the claim, stated first
THE POINT — 'the reason being': the justification, after the claim
there's no time — closed by からです, obligatorily
nazenara.note: から and ので put the reason first; なぜなら lets you claim first and justify after — the order an argument wants. It MUST close with からです.

wr.t: なぜかというと is its conversational cousin, same contract: open the reason, close with から. Leaving off the から breaks the frame in both.
wr.jp: なぜかというと、経験がないからです。
wr.en: The reason is that I have no experience.

items.q: 私は反対です。___、時間がないからです。
items.en: I'm against it, because there isn't time.
items.why: Claim first, reason after.

items.q: これが一番いいです。なぜなら、安全だ___です。
items.en: This is best, the reason being it's safe.
items.why: なぜなら must close with からです.

items.q: ___かというと、経験がないからです。
items.en: The reason is that I have no experience.
items.why: なぜかというと — the spoken frame.

items.q: 早く出ました。___、間に合いませんでした。
items.en: Left early. And yet — didn't make it.
items.why: An overturn, not a justification.

items.q: この店をすすめます。___、安くておいしいからです。
items.en: I recommend this place — because it's cheap and good.
items.why: The recommendation, then its grounds.

seg: THE POINT — 'for a': measured against its own kind, and off the standard
that went well — the compliment with a limit inside
nishiteha.note: Judges against the standard FOR ITS CATEGORY: good, for a beginner. The compliment and the ceiling arrive in the same breath.

wr.t: One kana away, にしても CONCEDES and presses on: 忙しいにしても、連絡はできたはず — even granting the busy-ness, the message was possible. Measure versus concede — the pair to keep apart.
wr.jp: 忙しいにしても、連絡はできたはずです。
wr.en: Busy or not, you could have got in touch.

items.q: 初めて___、よくできました。
items.en: For a first attempt, that went well.
items.why: Measured against first-attempt standards.

items.q: 冬___、暖かいですね。
items.en: It's warm for winter.
items.why: The season's own baseline, beaten.

items.q: 値段___、いい品物です。
items.en: For the price, a good item.
items.why: The price set the expectation; the goods exceeded it.

items.q: 忙しい___、連絡はできたはずです。
items.en: Even granting you were busy, you could have written.
items.why: Concession-then-press → にしても.

items.q: 子ども___、難しい言葉をよく知っていますね。
items.en: For a child, he knows some hard words.
items.why: Off the standard for his category — the raised eyebrow.

seg: busy — the point about to be conceded
THE POINT — even granting that: concede, then press on
連絡はできたはずです。
the message was still possible — the press
nishitemo.note: Grants the excuse its full weight and then presses the point anyway. Doubled, it covers both branches: 行くにしても行かないにしても.

wr.t: The doubled form collects what both worlds owe: 行くにしても行かないにしても、早く決めて — going or not, the deciding is due either way.
wr.jp: 行くにしても行かないにしても、早く決めて。
wr.en: Going or not, decide soon.

items.q: 忙しい___、連絡はできたはずです。
items.en: Even granting the busy-ness — a message was possible.
items.why: Concede, then press.

items.q: 行く___行かないにしても、早く決めて。
items.en: Going or not, decide soon.
items.why: The doubled concession, both branches billed.

items.q: 高い___、必要なものです。
items.en: Expensive though it may be, we need it.
items.why: The price granted; the need pressed.

items.q: 初めて___、よくできました。
items.en: For a first attempt, well done — measuring, not conceding.
items.why: Category standard → にしては.

items.q: 冗談___、言っていいことと悪いことがある。
items.en: Even as a joke, some things shouldn't be said.
items.why: The excuse granted whole, the line held anyway.

seg: THE POINT — instead of: substitution, or exchange
kawarini.note: Two senses easier together than apart: SUBSTITUTION (this rather than that) and EXCHANGE (this, but in return that). The second builds small social contracts.

wr.t: The exchange sense sets terms: 手伝う代わりに、夕食をおごって — the help priced in dinner, amiably, and the pattern holds the invoice.
wr.jp: 手伝う代わりに、夕食をおごってください。
wr.en: I'll help — in return, dinner's on you.

items.q: バターの___に油を使いました。
items.en: I used oil instead of butter.
items.why: Plain substitution.

items.q: 手伝う___に、夕食をおごってください。
items.en: I'll help — in return, dinner.
items.why: The exchange sense — terms set.

items.q: 行けない___に、手紙を書きます。
items.en: Since I can't go, I'll write instead.
items.why: The substitute offered for the absence.

items.q: 社長___に、ご挨拶いたします。
items.en: I'll speak on the president's behalf — standing in, not swapping goods.
items.why: Formal stand-in → にかわって; の代わりに trades things.

items.q: コーヒーの___に、お茶をどうぞ。
items.en: Have tea instead of coffee.
items.why: The offered substitute.

drill.note: The joints of a paragraph, most of them sentence-initial: つまり (restate), ところが (overturn), 一方で (balance), なぜなら〜からだ (justify after the claim), そこで／そのため as the neutral therefores. Learner writing reads as beads on a string until these arrive.

items.q: 安いと思った。___、高かった。
items.en: Reverse — the expectation broke.
items.why: The overturn joint.

items.q: 便利な___で、高いです。
items.en: Balance — both true at once.
items.why: The ledger's two sides.

items.q: 反対です。___、時間がないからです。
items.en: Justify — claim first, reason after.
items.why: The argument's order.

items.q: ___、そういうことです。
items.en: Restate — in short.
items.why: The summary joint.

items.q: 雨だった。___、試合は中止になった。
items.en: Therefore — the neutral consequence.
items.why: Cause carried forward without drama.

drill.note: The siblings you already own: the last N3-list items are one-move variations on taught shapes — べき negated, たとえ〜ても, だけでなく〜も, にしては／にしても one kana apart. Build them from what you hold; memorize nothing new.

items.q: そんなことを言う___ではありません。
items.en: You shouldn't say that — べき, negated.
items.why: The negative rides べき.

items.q: ___雨が降っても、行きます。
items.en: Even if it rains, I'm going.
items.why: たとえ〜ても — the concession flagged in advance.

items.q: 安い___でなく、質もいいです。
items.en: Not only cheap — good quality too.
items.why: だけでなく〜も — the widening pair.

items.q: 初めて___、上手ですね。
items.en: Good, for a first-timer — the measuring kana.
items.why: は measures; も concedes.

items.q: 高い___、買います。
items.en: Even granting it's expensive, I'll buy it.
items.why: The conceding kana.
